findings.description: The new temp-path allowance accepts glob operands such as `/tmp/*` before the existing catastrophic/glob checks run. `_fr2_temp_path_re='^/(tmp|var/tmp|private/tmp)/[^/]'` matches `/tmp/*`, and the loop immediately `continue`s, so `rm -rf /tmp/*` is allowed despite the fence previously treating glob roots as catastrophic and the new comments promising positively established temp paths, not wildcard wipes.
findings.failure_mode: A destructive command can delete every entry under a shared temp root while bypassing FR-2-BLOCK. This is a production-impact safety regression for the destructive-command fence.
findings.suggested_fix: Before the temp-root `continue`, reject glob/metacharacter operands (`*`, `?`, `[`, `$`, backticks, backslashes, spaces) or route them through the existing block-list first. Add dangerous corpus rows for `/tmp/*`, `/var/tmp/*`, and `/private/tmp/*`.
